newsitem.title: THAILAND: INTERVIEW-Srithai to focus on car part business.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Srithai to focus on car part business.

text.p: Thailand's largest plastic and melamine manufacturer, Srithai Superware Plc, said on Tuesday it planned to focus more of its business on car parts due to good prospects for the automotive industry.
"We are interested in producing plastic car parts for the automotive industry. The Thai car industry has a very high potential," Srithai president Sanan Ang-ubolkul told Reuters in an interview.

Sanan said the number of cars assembled in Thailand is expected to reach one million units by the year 2000. Total passenger and commercial vehicles assembled in Thailand was around 550,000 units last year.
"We will also supply auto parts for car makers in the Asian region," Sanan said.
General Motors Corp had chosen Srithai to produce the plastic bumper for its new Opel car assembled in Thailand, Sanan said.
"We will supply all plastic bumpers for GM's Opel cars. We are also negotiating with them to provide other parts," he said.
GM has invested $750 million in a new regional manufacturing facility to be located in Thailand's Eastern Seaboard region, eastern of Bangkok.
The facility, which is scheduled to be completed in early 1999, would produce about 100,000-150,000 Opel Asian cars of which 80 percent will be for export.
Srithai expects to see a 10 percent rise in its revenue in 1997 to 4.0 billion baht ($154 million) from 3.68 billion in the previous year despite the country's sagging economy, Sanan said.
"The revenue rise will be boosted by higher demand from U.S. and Japan markets. There has been a large number of orders from both countries since late last year," he said.
Sanan said Srithai will expand its businesses into other neighbouring countries in the region to catch up with their economic growth.
Srithai has built a 150 million baht plant in Vietnam to produce plastic crates for soft drinks and beer, he said.
"The demand in Vietnam is very high. We are looking for a site to build a new plant to double our production capacity," he said.
The new factory will also make melamine plates and bowls, he said.
Srithai will also jointly invest with Mitsui & Co to build a plastic and melamine plant in Burma.
The Burma plant will need an investment of about 100 million baht and be completed next year, he said.
